newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe rapeseed steady, flood regions may import.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe rapeseed steady, flood regions may import.

text.p: Rapeseed prices in Northern Europe are under pressure as a large domestic harvest nears but hopes of exports to flood-affected eastern Europe are offsetting negative impact, brokers said on Friday.
New crop buyers for ex-harvest seed were broadly steady at 432.50 marks/tonne free Hamburg, they reported.
Farmers in eastern Germany have already marketed large parts of their crop locally ahead of harvesting while western German traders and merchants are not as interested in local supplies.
Traders and analysts said Poland's rapeseed crop in 1997 may fall to 350,000-370,000 tonnes versus earlier forecasts for 400,000 tonnes as a result of flooding in the south.
Traders said while this presented opportunities for western European rapeseed, there would be competition from eastern European sunseed and rapeseed.
For instance, it was unclear whether rapeseed producers in the Czech republic had suffered from flooding or whether the country would be able to harvest a surplus and export to Poland.
Another uncertainty is the 15 percent Polish import tariff, which prospective sellers hope may be lifted because the flood has created food supply gaps.
There was talk Poland might need 350,000-400,000 tonnes of rapeseed imports in 1997/98 and that Canada might be able to supply up to 150,000 tonnes of canola from its new crop at the end of 1997.
In Germany, rapeseed harvesting began in south eastern Germany but had to be interrupted when heavy showers set in.
Rapeseed prices for delivery at points other than Hamburg were in a 422.50-435 marks range for July, little changed from last week.
November rapeseed on the Matif futures traded at 442 marks, up two from Thursday's close and up 10 from last week.
July rape meal was no longer quoted while Aug/Oct meal was off one mark/100 kg on the week at 22.75 and Nov/Jan 0.25 lower at 24.50.
Rape oil sellers prices were at 92.75 marks for August, down from 93.75 last quoted for July, while Aug/Oct oil was at 93.50, up three.
